examples.question_text: A rectangular food container has internal dimensions $15$ cm by $10$ cm by $8$ cm. Find its capacity in litres.
examples.solution_text:
Calculate the volume.
$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(15\times10)\times8\\&=1200\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Convert to capacity using $1\text{ cm}^{3}=1\text{ mL}$.
$\begin{aligned}C&=1200\text{ mL}\\&=1.2\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A trough has a right-triangular cross-section with perpendicular sides $30$ cm and $40$ cm. Its internal length is $120$ cm. Find its capacity in litres.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont,text=black},draw=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(0,3)--cycle;\draw (0.25,0)--(0.25,0.25)--(0,0.25);\path (2,0) node[below] {$40\text{ cm}$};\path (0,1.5) node[left] {$30\text{ cm}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
examples.solution_text:
Find the triangular cross-section area, then multiply by the length.
$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{40\times30}{2}\\&=600\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=600\times120\\&=72\,000\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Convert to capacity.
$\begin{aligned}C&=72\,000\text{ mL}\\&=72\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A cylindrical container has internal radius $4$ cm and height $12$ cm. Find its capacity in millilitres, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont,text=black},draw=black]\draw (-1.2,0)--(-1.2,3.6);\draw (1.2,0)--(1.2,3.6);\draw (0,3.6) ellipse (1.2 and 0.35);\draw (-1.2,0) arc[start angle=180,end angle=360,x radius=1.2,y radius=0.35];\draw[dashed] (-1.2,0) arc[start angle=180,end angle=0,x radius=1.2,y radius=0.35];\fill[black] (0,3.6) circle (1.5pt);\draw (0,3.6)--(1.2,3.6);\path (0.6,3.6) node[above,fill=white,inner sep=1pt] {$4\text{ cm}$};\path (1.2,1.8) node[right] {$12\text{ cm}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
examples.solution_text:
Calculate the volume.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times4^{2}\times12\\&=192\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Convert to capacity, then round.
$\begin{aligned}C&=192\pi\text{ mL}\\&\approx603.19\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A cylindrical tank has internal diameter $2$ m and height $1.5$ m. Find its capacity in litres, correct to the nearest litre.
examples.solution_text:
The radius is half the diameter.
$\begin{aligned}r&=2\div2\\&=1\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times1^{2}\times1.5\\&=1.5\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Use $1\text{ m}^{3}=1000\text{ L}$.
$\begin{aligned}C&=1500\pi\text{ L}\\&\approx4712\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A $2.5$ L bottle of juice is poured into cylindrical glasses with internal radius $3$ cm and height $10$ cm. How many full glasses can be filled?
examples.solution_text:
Find the capacity of one glass.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times3^{2}\times10\\&=90\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Each glass holds $90\pi$ mL. The bottle contains $2500$ mL.
$\begin{aligned}N&=\frac{2500}{90\pi}\\&\approx8.84\end{aligned}$
Round down: $8$ full glasses can be filled.

examples.question_text: A cylindrical drum with internal radius $15$ cm and height $40$ cm is full of water. A gardener uses $12$ L. Find how much water remains, in litres, correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Calculate the drum's volume and capacity.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times15^{2}\times40\\&=9000\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}C&=9000\pi\text{ mL}\\&=9\pi\text{ L}\end{aligned}$
Subtract the water used before rounding.
$\begin{aligned}R&=9\pi-12\\&\approx16.3\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A planter is a right prism with the trapezium cross-section shown and internal length $30$ cm. A bag contains $6$ L of potting mix. Is it enough to fill the planter? State the surplus or shortfall in litres.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont,text=black},draw=black]\draw (0,0)--(2.8,0)--(3.5,2)--(-0.7,2)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (1.4,0)--(1.4,2);\draw (1.4,0.2)--(1.6,0.2)--(1.6,0);\path (1.4,0) node[below] {$14\text{ cm}$};\path (1.4,2) node[above] {$21\text{ cm}$};\path (1.4,1) node[right,fill=white,inner sep=1pt] {$10\text{ cm}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
examples.solution_text:
Find the cross-section area and volume.
$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{10(21+14)}{2}\\&=175\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=175\times30\\&=5250\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
The planter holds $5250$ mL, or $5.25$ L.
$\begin{aligned}S&=6-5.25\\&=0.75\text{ L}\end{aligned}$
The bag is enough, with $0.75$ L to spare.

examples.question_text: A rectangular tank has internal dimensions $1.2$ m by $50$ cm by $40$ cm. Water enters at $2$ L every $20$ seconds. How long does it take to fill the empty tank, in minutes?
examples.solution_text:
Use centimetres for all dimensions: $1.2\text{ m}=120\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(120\times50)\times40\\&=240\,000\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
The tank holds $240\,000$ mL, or $240$ L.
There are $3$ periods of $20$ seconds in a minute.
$\begin{aligned}q&=2\times3\\&=6\text{ L/min}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}t&=240\div6\\&=40\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A juice carton has internal dimensions $9$ cm by $10$ cm by $20$ cm. It is $70\%$ full. Each cup holds $250$ mL. How many full cups can be filled?
examples.solution_text:
Find the carton's full capacity.
$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(9\times10)\times20\\&=1800\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Its full capacity is $1800$ mL.
$\begin{aligned}J&=0.70\times1800\\&=1260\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}N&=1260\div250\\&=5.04\end{aligned}$
Round down: $5$ full cups can be filled.

examples.question_text: Container A is a cylinder with internal radius $6$ cm and height $15$ cm. Container B is a rectangular prism with internal dimensions $12$ cm by $10$ cm by $13$ cm. Which holds more, and by how many litres, correct to $2$ decimal places?
examples.solution_text:
Calculate each volume.
$\begin{aligned}V_A&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times6^{2}\times15\\&=540\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}V_B&=Ah\\&=(12\times10)\times13\\&=1560\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Their capacities are $0.54\pi$ L and $1.56$ L respectively.
$\begin{aligned}D&=0.54\pi-1.56\\&\approx0.14\text{ L}\end{aligned}$
Container A holds more, by $0.14$ L.

examples.question_text: During a storm, $30$ mm of rain falls on a flat rectangular roof measuring $10$ m by $7$ m. All runoff is collected. How many litres of water are collected?
examples.solution_text:
Treat the rainfall as a rectangular prism with depth $30\text{ mm}=0.03\text{ m}$.
$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(10\times7)\times0.03\\&=2.1\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$
Convert to capacity.
$\begin{aligned}C&=2.1\text{ kL}\\&=2100\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Base area = 15 × 10 = 150 cm²; volume = 150 × 8 = 1200 cm³; capacity = 1200 mL = 1.2 L.
The diagram marks perpendicular 40 cm and 30 cm sides. Cross-section area = 40 × 30 ÷ 2 = 600 cm²; volume = 600 × 120 = 72000 cm³; capacity = 72 L.
Volume = π × 4² × 12 = 192π cm³; capacity = 192π mL ≈ 603.19 mL. The diagram identifies the radius and height correctly.
Radius = 2 ÷ 2 = 1 m; volume = π × 1² × 1.5 = 1.5π m³; capacity = 1500π L ≈ 4712 L to the nearest litre.
One glass holds π × 3² × 10 = 90π mL. Available juice = 2500 mL; 2500 ÷ (90π) ≈ 8.84, allowing 8 full glasses.
Drum volume = π × 15² × 40 = 9000π cm³; capacity = 9π L. Remaining water = 9π − 12 ≈ 16.2743 L, rounding to 16.3 L.
The diagram supplies parallel sides 21 cm and 14 cm and perpendicular height 10 cm. Area = 10(21 + 14) ÷ 2 = 175 cm²; volume = 175 × 30 = 5250 cm³ = 5.25 L. Surplus = 6 − 5.25 = 0.75 L.
Convert 1.2 m to 120 cm. Volume = 120 × 50 × 40 = 240000 cm³ = 240 L. Flow rate = 2 × 3 = 6 L/min; filling time = 240 ÷ 6 = 40 minutes.
Full capacity = 9 × 10 × 20 = 1800 mL. Juice available = 0.70 × 1800 = 1260 mL; 1260 ÷ 250 = 5.04, allowing 5 full cups.
Cylinder capacity = π × 6² × 15 ÷ 1000 = 0.54π L ≈ 1.69646 L. Prism capacity = 12 × 10 × 13 ÷ 1000 = 1.56 L. Container A holds approximately 0.13646 L more, rounding to 0.14 L.
Rainfall depth = 30 mm = 0.03 m. Collected volume = 10 × 7 × 0.03 = 2.1 m³; capacity = 2.1 kL = 2100 L.
